title: Module pullback and pushforward adjunction on arbitrary ringed topoi
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites, with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$, and let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi, an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits, equipped with a ring map $c:u^{-1}R\to S$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] put $u^*M=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For an $S$-module sheaf $H$, give $u_*H$ its $R$-module structure via the adjunct $R\to u_*S$ of $c$. There are canonical bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_S(u^*M,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,u_*H)$, natural in $M,H$. Thus the displayed tensor-formula pullback is left adjoint to this module pushforward.

proof.text: Transport the sheaf of rings R to A with its underlying isomorphism and the stated operation comparisons.
For each c:A→S, obtain I,P and the natural linear hom equivalence B, together with the underlying normalization.

Construct the presheaf scalar-extension functor from the sectionwise tensor products. Restriction on a pure tensor is the specified change-of-rings restriction. The ordinary extension/restriction hom equivalence gives maps in both directions; equality on pure tensors proves their naturality with respect to site restrictions and their inverse identities.

Compose with module sheafification. Its universal hom equivalence identifies maps from the sheafified tensor with maps from the tensor presheaf. The unit on sections is the sheafification unit applied to 1⊗m, and its naturality identifies the induced underlying map with restriction along this unit.

Define T as I followed by this explicit scalar-extension functor. Compose the scalar-extension hom equivalence with B and prove its two naturality equations. Use Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv. The tensor object and map identifications are definitional; combine the scalar-extension unit formula and the normalization for B to obtain the last required equation.

lean.note: Section 1(B). The general theorem is publicly reexported unchanged. Its equal-universe presentation cannot instantiate the actual small pro-etale site, and does not expose the normalized adjunction for the completed, potentially noninvertible coefficient structure maps. This module supplies that specialization with its literal tensor-unit section formula, derived adjunction, normalized shifts and canonical complete reflector. The module reuses the now-published completed ordinary pullback and direct image, rather than a private choice of derived functors.
